questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that the destination was vastly different than Denmark, preferably both in culture and nature. It is a plus that the education is in english as it made learning and communication easier. That the destination had a good study culture, and a good university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. As soon as you were on campus everything was much easier than online

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Their help center (STOP 1) was always good at troubleshooting, and helped me with my health insurrance

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is not easy to find an affordable place. Everyone uses the facebook site "fairy floss real estate".

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Do not go for student housing such as scape or unilodge if possible. They are really unaffordable and feels like living in a cheap hotel. 
If possible try to find a share house!!!
It was through my share house i got most of my friends, and a good way to meet local Australians

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a bit overwhelming trying to find the right information on their website, and which subjects i could enroll in

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Call STOP 1! I did that several times and they were always very kind and helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It is hard to expect which subjects are good. I ended up changing some after some time. When you get to the campus it is easier to get a feel for the subjects.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Call them when in doubt! i ended up spending too much time exploring the wrong parts of their website

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Depends on which subjects you take. I went for a few subjects that was pretty different from my programm and they ended up being pretty hard. The biotechnology courses was somewhat the same level as at home

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: No books, not much reading in general, and a lot of recorded lectures. A lot of assignments that had to be handed in every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Protein Structure and Function BCMB30001
Australia in the Wine World AGRI10039
Biology of Australian Flora and Fauna BIOL10001
Philosophy of Science HPSC 20026

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
loved the wine subject (although the eksam was horrific)
I loved learning about Australian flora and fauna. highly recomenable!! They had many good professors 

The Protein subject was hard, and it only had prerecorded lectures, but besides that the subject was really interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My share house came unfurnished and had to invest in a lot of things. I had a spontanious Japan trip which also were expensive

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
grocery shopping is expensive. Buying food out is a bit cheaper than Denmark.
Local transport is also expensive. I ended up buying a bike

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were a lot of different clubs you could join and a great way of meeting other exchange students. 
If you are into sports they had almost every sport you could imagine, including scupa diving. Otherewise there were a lot of cultural clubs, some more niche than others.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The surf club! I got a lot of my friends through their trips. It is very popular so you have to be lucky to get on one of their trips:/ 
The wine club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Deffinetly go out and see some nature around melbourne. If you can hire a car, you can get to some pretty amazing places fairly easily. Wilsons promotory, the grampians and great ocean road are some nice close locations

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: really easy! Aussies are usually very warm and welcoming

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not a lot of socializing happens in or around the class room. If you want to meet students you have to join the clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not any really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It does not take as much to become friends with someone. they are usually really open and welcoming

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join clubs that rely on socializing
Try to set of time to explore australia (especially by car)
Find a sharehouse

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: they have a free food arrangement which is pretty handy

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Establishing a network of people from scratch in another country was really rewarding, as you know that you still have a connection to that country and something you can go back to

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: finding ways to meet new people! the uni is not nescecarily great when it comes to socializing and meeting people

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
